q: Which Vitest option runs only the tests whose name matches a pattern?
why: -t (or --testNamePattern) filters by test name. In the lesson's run, 1 test ran and 6 were skipped.

q: What do you need to test a React component with Vitest?
why: React needs a page to draw on, which jsdom provides, and React Testing Library to render the component and use it like a user. A real browser is only needed for end to end tests, and Supertest is for API routes.

q: Why do you put app.listen in a different file than the Express app for Supertest?
options: So tests can import the app without starting a server on a port
Because Supertest cannot read the app otherwise
Because Express forbids listen in the app file
why: If the app file calls listen, every test file starts a real server on the same port and you get address already in use. Export the app, listen in server.js, and test with request(app).

q: In a Playwright test, you should add await page.waitForTimeout(3000) before each check so the page has time to load.
why: No. Playwright's expect waits and retries until the thing is true. A fixed sleep makes tests slow and still flaky.

q: What does the webServer setting in playwright.config do?
options: Starts your app before the tests and waits until its address answers
Records a trace of each test
why: webServer takes a command to start the app and a url to wait for. Playwright starts it, runs the tests, then stops it.

q: The Next.js docs recommend what for testing an async Server Component?
why: Some unit test tools do not fully support async Server Components yet, so the docs recommend end to end tests for them. Unit test the plain functions and synchronous components.
